The availability of employment opportunities and the resultant population growth are the primary factors in any socio-economic impact analyses. Therefore, these will be the basis of the impact assessment which follows. First, comparisons of these two factors will be made between Westmoreland Resources' most probable coal production level (Scenario 1) and the 26 million tons per year shipment level (Scenario 2). The analysis considers variations in peripheral coal development and labor participation rates, and the discussion will include consideration of the changes in the degree or intensity of the resulting socio-economic impacts. The projected changes in employment will continue to be presented in terms of total employment which includes increases in basic non-agricultural employment (essentially all employment directly associated with coal development) plus all changes in non-basic employment which would be generated as a result of the increased activity stimulated by coal development. As can be seen in Figure III-11, the higher production level (Scenario 2) is essentially a continuation and an expansion of Scenario 1.
Projected employment growth, both Crow and Non-Crow, is identical for both scenarios until 1988, when employment levels for Scenario 2 begin to noticeably exceed those for Scenario 1. For Scenario 2, projected non-Indian employment exceeds 3100 in 1988, peaks in 1990 at about 3200 employees, and then remains relatively stable until the year 2000. The total employee increase attributable to Westmoreland Resources operations is 3298 compared to 3164 for the more probable level. This is an increase of 4.2% in non-Indian employment resulting from the higher production level.
